video_title: Biggest NBA Trades and Free Agency Takeaways No One Else is Talking About

quotes.speaker: James Herbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Mo Wagner's potential as an undervalued asset for the Nets
quotes.excerpt: If you're the Nets, you want to try to buy low on guys that might be undervalued.
quotes.quote: If you're the Nets, you want to try to buy low on guys that might be undervalued for certain reasons. Maybe that's Mo Wagner. Maybe that's a good move by the Nets. I don't know, we'll have to see how he is next year.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the second apron on NBA team building
quotes.excerpt: It feels like the big boogeyman of the NBA is finally here, the monster is out.
quotes.quote: Three years in after the 2023 CBA, it feels like the big boogeyman of the NBA is finally here, the monster is out of the closet. Everybody is super scared of the second apron. And we've seen that a little bit to this point. It's effectively, agents have been calling it a hard cap since it went into effect. I think some teams have been treating it that way too.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' strategic avoidance of the second apron
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks, when James Dolan goes out and says on radio that it would be suicidal.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: When James Dolan, the New York Knicks owner, goes out and says on radio that it would be suicidal to go into the second apron. The Knicks, who once spent to no end, who did not care about what their salary cap looked like, are now unwilling to go into the second apron.

text_blocks.speaker: James Herbert
text_blocks.text: I think the Knicks are too scared, or the Knicks are too cheap, or something. I don't get it from all the reporting that's out there. It seems like the front office was planning to go into the second apron because, as you said, if not now, when would you do it? This is the perfect time to go into the second apron when all that it is really costing you is temporarily a higher luxury tax bill.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Teams are avoiding the second apron to maintain roster flexibility
quotes.excerpt: You want to pick your moment in time that you want to go over the second apron.
quotes.quote: You want to pick your moment in time that you want to go over the second apron. You want to pick two years, go in, take your shot, get out. Now, the Cavs were the only team in the second apron for the 2025-26 season. They're out of it as of right now. We'll see what the Thunder do. Maybe they ultimately end up staying there, maybe they don't.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The Hornets' strategic pivot with the LaMelo Ball trade
quotes.excerpt: I think the Hornets, the more I've thought about this LaMelo Ball trade, I first my reaction.
quotes.quote: I think the Hornets, the more I've thought about this LaMelo Ball trade, I first my reaction was mass confusion on both sides. I get what the Timberwolves are doing. I think it's interesting. They've increased their level of variance. We're going to see how much we can kind of increase the ceiling on this team. And LaMelo Ball is our way to do it. And if it hits, you have a great playmaker. You have someone who's going to increase your three-point shooting, your ability to score with the best teams out there. And obviously, it takes some of the load off of Anthony Edwards, so I don't think he'll be able to be defended the way that he was.

quotes.speaker: James Herbert
quotes.summary_phrase: The Hornets' identity and LaMelo Ball's influence on their playstyle
quotes.excerpt: The Hornets were my favorite team in the league to watch last year.
quotes.quote: The Hornets were my favorite team in the league to watch last year. A lot of that was LaMelo and the verb that he plays with, the style that he has, the crazy shots that he would take and sometimes make, and the shots that he would create for others, and just sort of the pace that he injects into the game. Not necessarily just by running, just like the speed at which they did things in the half court.

quotes.speaker: James Herbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe White's consistent performance regardless of lineup changes
quotes.excerpt: Kobe White's minutes are pretty much regardless of who is on the floor with him.
quotes.quote: Kobe White's minutes are pretty much regardless of who is on the floor with him. They were good, and Kobe White's minutes are pretty much regardless of who is on the floor with him. So I do think they're still going to be a good team. They're going to be a different team.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The Hornets' draft capital and potential for future roster moves
quotes.excerpt: The Hornets had enough I think draft picks before this trade even.
quotes.quote: The Hornets had enough I think draft picks before this trade even. They could have gone the other way. They could have sold a story to themselves like, hey, we get in the Jaylen Brown market, right? Our contracts, Brandon Miller still on his rookie deal, Kobe White obviously entering year two. They got a few young draft picks. You could have gone the other way and said, all right, we can take on three years of Jaylen Brown before we get to two big extensions on our cap sheet, and we can work that through.

quotes.speaker: James Herbert
quotes.summary_phrase: The Wizards' playoff prospects after their draft moves
quotes.excerpt: Do you think the Wizards are making the playoffs? It's possible, but I don't like project that.
quotes.quote: Do you think the Wizards are making the playoffs? It's possible, but I don't like project that when I look at all these other teams in the Eastern Conference. The Indiana Pacers were the second worst team in the East last year. I have no idea how good they're going to be next year, but I'm assuming Tyrese Haliburton is going to be playing at an All-NBA level again.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The Warriors' status as title contenders depends on Anthony Davis
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors are no longer considered like one of the favorites unless they get Anthony Davis.
quotes.quote: I saw Shams reported today that the Warriors are no longer considered like one of the favorites unless they get Anthony Davis. And I think it would be kind of crazy if they got Anthony Davis.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The perception of Jaylen Brown's value in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The league does not value Jaylen Brown to the degree that maybe we on the outside.
quotes.quote: Everyone seems to be of the perception that the league does not value Jaylen Brown to the degree that maybe we on the outside thought we did. I remember talking to one assistant general manager when he was about to get his max extension that just said plainly, I would not have given that contract. They did not value him as a max player. Yet, he did, and he won a Finals MVP. This so that means he contributed to winning.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the second apron on team building and player movement
quotes.excerpt: The second apron is in place and is used as a cudgel by owners to their fans.
quotes.quote: I think now the second apron is in place and is used as a cudgel by owners to their fans and to their teams from keeping. And I think that to me is a significant difference in how those high spenders do and do not act anymore.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential fit with the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: Had he gone to the Warriors before the season that we just saw him have, it would have been sort of weird
quotes.quote: Had he gone to the Warriors before the season that we just saw him have, where he actually transitioned to more of an off-ball role consistently for the first time in his career, it would have been sort of weird to figure out how this works. He is going to want to play LeBron ball, but they want to play Warriors ball. He has always been more than smart enough to do so, he gets it. He has spent enough time thinking about how they play and defending it, and he is one of the smartest players ever to play. He could figure it out.

quotes.speaker: James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' risk of repeating the Michael Jordan Wizards era
quotes.excerpt: If he goes anywhere but the Heat and the Cavaliers, there is a LeBron risk creating his Jordan on the Wizards era.
quotes.quote: If he goes anywhere but the Heat and the Cavaliers, there is a LeBron risk creating his Jordan on the Wizards era. It is a possibility. Even if he goes to the Heat or the Cavaliers and then he has this weird injury-riddled season and it is sort of forgettable, then that is the equivalent of the Jordan Wizards era. He just happens to be wearing a familiar uniform. I do not think he cares. This phase of his life, he is turning 42 in December. He has surpassed every expectation of how long he would play and how effective he would still be at this age.

quotes.speaker: James
quotes.summary_phrase: Prioritizing player experience over team legacy in free agency
quotes.excerpt: I think we care too much about legacy because that is an us thing, and I think it's more important how the player experiences their career.
quotes.quote: I think we care too much about legacy because that is an us thing, and I think it's more important how the player experiences their career. Because that is a them thing, and that is what is probably more important for them is how they experience their career, where they go, what they do, more than what their legacy is. Because you can be as good as you can be, you can be as good as LeBron, and you can still not wholly control your legacy. So I think it is probably more important to just do what you want to do.

quotes.speaker: James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James as an astute observer of sports media
quotes.excerpt: When LeBron James retires, we are going to miss the most astute media observer in professional sports history.
quotes.quote: When LeBron James retires, we are going to miss the most astute media observer in professional sports history. He is one of the most astute media observers out there right now because if you look at the way that LeBron James has handled every one of his free agencies, it has been this really smart understanding of where media and eyeballs are at that point in time. People like to talk about how every election is defined by a new media company or a new media platform that is emerging, and it shows where people are. I think LeBron James' free agency does a better job of that than anything else.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Hypothetical LeBron James return to the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: I feel like it would be very cleansing to the people of Ohio to have the decision go the other way.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: So let's say he goes back to Cleveland. What do you think of this? He does the decision too. It is on streaming now, and just like the first time, Donovan Mitchell is there wearing a Boys & Girls Club shirt.

text_blocks.speaker: James
text_blocks.text: I feel like it would be very cleansing to the people of Ohio to have the decision go the other way. The decision too, updated 16 years later for 2026, has to be on streaming. Instead of Jim Gray, it has to be another athlete interviewing him as part of his podcast, or he does it for the Mind the Game podcast. It is like self-content. That would be the refresh on that whole situation.
